2.text: and travelled along it for two weeks. Then he had an encounter with the

3.text: Chukchee. Three battles were fought in the course of a month. The Chukchee

4.text: were defeated. Pavlutsky turned to the Bay of Anadyr, and reached Anadyrsk

5.text: on Oct. 21. According to other information, Pavlutsky took a great number

6.text: of reindeer, also about three hundred Chukchee women, who, however, all

7.text: perished on the way to Yakutsk. Notwithstanding all such captures, Chukchee

8.text: female prisoners are but rarely mentioned in the lists of population of those

9.text: districts, of which we have several referring to the period spoken of. Thus,

10.text: in the register of 1762, among the population of Nishne-Kolymsk is mentioned

11.text: one captive woman, a Chukchee native, Liliˊña. In the documents of 1811

12.text: is mentioned an old Cossack widow, Krasnoyarov, born a Chukchee woman,

14.text: In 1738 about two thousand Chukchee, armed with bows, made a raid

15.text: against the Koryak of the Anadyr district, killed many, and drove off their

16.text: reindeer-herds. In 1741 the Cabinet Council of Russia resolved to increase

17.text: the garrison of Anadyrsk and to renew the war. The Cossack party soon

18.text: gained such a victory over the Chukchee, that the Cossacks were able to

19.text: replace the hard bread for three months and a half with dried meat captured

20.text: from the Chukchee. The garrison included four hundred Cossacks and

21.text: one hundred other men, besides the exiled criminals who also were sent to

22.text: Anadyr until March of the year 1764. In the year 1747 the Chukchee

23.text: began again to make inroads into the Koryak territory. On March 21,

24.text: Pavlutsky went in pursuit of a large Chukchee party. He bade the main

25.text: body of his soldiers to follow behind, and he himself went forward, having

26.text: with him only eighty men. Soon he overtook the enemy, who were very

27.text: numerous, standing on the hill, The Russians held a council. One lieutenant

28.text: proposed to wait for the other party; but the other lieutenant, Gornitzyn, said

29.text: angrily, “It seems that our Cossacks are warlike only at home, and in

30.text: battle they are weak-hearted. The present is the time to strike the enemy.”

31.text: So they rushed onward, but a part of the Chukchee caught them from behind.

32.text: A part of the Cossacks fled with driving-reindeer, and escaped the peril.

33.text: Pavlutsky and some others fought valiantly, but were all killed. The hill

34.text: here mentioned is, according to tradition, the Yukaghir Hill not far from

35.text: Markova. The other stories mentioned before agree well with this historical

36.text: account, and give even the same name of the lieutenant, who goaded the

37.text: Cossacks on to battle. According to the tradition, he was the first to flee

39.text: The war continued after Pavlutsky’s defeat. The next year, 1748, there

40.text: came to Anadyrsk a company of soldiers and some more Cossacks. In the

41.text: year 1752 a hundred soldiers were sent to Anadyrsk under Major Shmalev.
